title: 并联：每条路有自己的电流
summary: 两颗不同颜色的 LED 共用一个电阻，绿色的不亮。为什么？给每条支路一个自己的电阻就好了。
concepts: same voltage 两端电压相同
description: 并联的几条支路两端接在同样的两个结点上，所以两端电压相同，各自的电流由自己的元件决定，总电流是各支路电流之和。两颗颜色不同的 LED 不能共用一个限流电阻：压降低的那颗会把电压“卡住”，另一颗点不亮。

cards.title: 两颗灯共用一个电阻
text: 先搭红色 LED 和它的 150 Ω 电阻。然后把一颗**绿色** LED **并联**在红色 LED 旁边，共用同一个电阻。
看看两颗灯：哪颗亮，哪颗不亮？

cards.title: 并联：两端电压一样
text: - **并联**的两颗 LED 两端接在**同样的两个结点**上，所以它们两端的电压**必须相等**（还记得 KVL 实验里的回路 ② 吗）。
- 红色 LED 在 1.8 V 左右就导通，把这两个结点之间的电压**卡在约 2 V**。绿色 LED 要 2.1 V 才开始导通——电压不够，它就不亮。
- 解决办法：**每条支路一个自己的电阻**。这样每颗 LED 的电压由自己的支路决定，互不干扰：

cards.title: 每条支路一个电阻
text: 拿掉共用电阻的绿色 LED，给它单独搭一条支路。

cards.title: 带走
text: - 并联：**两端电压相同**，电流各走各的，**总电流 = 各支路电流之和**（这就是 KCL，下一个实验专门测它）。
- 家里的插座全是并联的：每个电器都拿到同样的 220 V（或 120 V），关掉一个不影响别的。
- 并联 LED 规则：**一颗 LED，一个电阻**。同颜色同型号的 LED 共用电阻也不保险——压降稍有差别，电流就会偏向一颗。

en.title: Parallel: every path has its own current
en.summary: Two LEDs of different colours share one resistor and the green one stays dark. Why? Give each branch its own resistor.
en.description: Parallel branches connect to the same two nodes, so they have the same voltage across them; each branch's current is set by its own parts, and the total current is the sum of the branch currents. Two LEDs of different colours cannot share one resistor: the one with the lower drop clamps the voltage and the other one never lights.
steps: **R1** (**`150 Ω`**): one leg straight into the red rail at **`tp5`**, the other in **`b5`**.
**Red LED1**: long lead **`c5`**, short lead **`c8`**; blue **jumper** **`a8`** → **`tn8`**. The red LED is lit.
**Green LED**: long lead **`d5`**, short lead **`d8`** — the same two columns as the red one, sharing R1. Are both lit?
Second branch: **R2** (**`150 Ω`**) with one leg in **`tp12`** and the other in **`b12`**.
**Green LED2**: long lead **`c12`**, short lead **`c15`**; blue **jumper** **`a15`** → **`tn15`**. Both branches start at the red rail and end at the blue rail: parallel.
Both are lit. Press **Check my circuit**, then **click each LED** and read its current in Properties.
hints: Each branch starts at the red rail and ends at the blue rail: the resistor's top leg in the red rail, the LED's short lead jumpered to the blue rail.
Green LED dark? Check whether it still shares a resistor with the red one.

cards.title: Two lights, one resistor
text: First build the red LED with its 150 Ω resistor. Then put a **green** LED **in parallel** with the red one, sharing the same resistor.
Look at both: which one lights, and which one does not?

cards.title: Parallel: the same voltage across
text: - Two LEDs **in parallel** connect to **the same two nodes**, so the voltage across them **must be equal** (remember loop ② in the KVL lab).
- The red LED conducts from about 1.8 V and **clamps the voltage between those nodes at about 2 V**. The green LED needs 2.1 V to start — not enough voltage, no light.
- The fix: **each branch gets its own resistor**. Then each LED's voltage is set by its own branch and they no longer interfere:

cards.title: One resistor per branch
text: Remove the green LED that shares the resistor and give it a branch of its own.

cards.title: Take away
text: - Parallel: **same voltage across**, each current goes its own way, **total current = sum of the branch currents** (that is KCL — the next lab measures it).
- The sockets in your home are all in parallel: every appliance gets the same mains voltage, and switching one off does not affect the others.
- Rule for parallel LEDs: **one LED, one resistor**. Even identical LEDs should not share one — a slight difference in their drops sends most of the current through one of them.

measurements.ask: In step 4, with both LEDs sharing one resistor, why did the green one stay dark?
choices: In parallel both see the same voltage; the red one clamps it at about 2 V, too little for green
measurements.explain: Parts in parallel share the same voltage. The red LED has the lower drop, conducts first and holds the voltage down; the 2.1 V the green one needs never arrives.

measurements.ask: Click the red LED1: the current in Properties
Click the green LED2: the current in Properties
measurements.explain: (5 − 2.1) / (150 + 12) ≈ 17.9 mA. Same voltage on both branches, different drops, different currents.

measurements.ask: From your two readings: how much current does the power module deliver in total?
measurements.explain: The two branch currents meet at the red rail, so the total is their sum — that is KCL.

measurements.ask: 第 4 步里两颗 LED 共用一个电阻时，为什么绿色的不亮？
choices: 并联时两颗灯两端电压相同，红灯把它卡在约 2 V，不够绿灯导通
measurements.explain: 并联元件两端电压相同。红灯的压降低，先导通，把电压限住；绿灯需要的 2.1 V 永远到不了。

measurements.ask: 单击红色 LED1：「属性」里显示的电流
单击绿色 LED2：「属性」里显示的电流
measurements.explain: (5 − 2.1) / (150 + 12) ≈ 17.9 mA。两条支路电压一样，压降不同，电流就不同。

measurements.ask: 用你的两个读数算：电源模块一共送出多少电流？
measurements.explain: 两条支路的电流在红轨汇合，总电流就是两者之和——这就是 KCL。

steps.text: **面包板电源模块**插 **`tp1`**，保持 **5 V**。
**绿色 LED**：长脚 **`d5`**、短脚 **`d8`**——和红灯插在同样的两列里，共用 R1。两颗灯都亮了吗？
选中**绿色 LED**，按 **Delete** 删掉。
**绿色 LED2**：长脚 **`c12`**、短脚 **`c15`**；蓝色**跳线** **`a15`** → **`tn15`**。两条支路的上端都在红轨、下端都在蓝轨：并联完成。
两颗都亮了。点**「检查我的电路」**，然后**单击每颗 LED**，在「属性」里读它的电流。

hints: 每条支路都要从红轨出发、回到蓝轨：电阻上端插红轨，LED 短脚用跳线接蓝轨。
绿色 LED 不亮？看看它是不是还和红色 LED 共用一个电阻。
